findings.title: Cache only successfully admitted devices
findings.body: tagDeviceUI adds the device to localCache before calling CreateOrUpdateDevice. When the store rejects a new device with ErrDeviceLimitReached, this return propagates the error but leaves the cache entry in place for 29 minutes. The next request with the same device ID hits the cache, returns nil, and receives an anonymous identity despite the limit still being reached. Only cache successful admissions, and ensure concurrent requests cannot treat an admission still in progress as successful.

findings.title: Requests without a device header bypass the limit
findings.body: Authenticate relies entirely on TagDevice returning ErrDeviceLimitReached to deny access, but TagDevice returns nil immediately when X-Grafana-Device-Id is absent. Consequently, even when the configured limit is full, a client can omit this client-controlled header and continue accessing anonymous APIs without being counted or rejected. Device admission must not be optional merely because the request omits its identifier.

findings.title: Make the device count check and admission atomic
findings.body: CountDevices runs in a separate database session from the subsequent unconditional upsert, with no serialization between them. For example, with a limit of one and an empty table, two concurrent requests for different devices can both observe zero devices and then both insert successfully. This also occurs across Grafana instances sharing the database. The count check and admission need database-level serialization or another atomic mechanism to prevent exceeding the configured cap.

findings.title: Register the setting before environment overrides are applied
findings.body: The PR reads device_limit here but does not add it to conf/defaults.ini. Grafana applies environment overrides to keys already present in the loaded INI before readAuthSettings runs, so creating this key here is too late. On an otherwise default configuration, GF_AUTH_ANONYMOUS_DEVICE_LIMIT is silently ignored and the limit remains zero, meaning unlimited devices. Add the default INI key or read this setting through an environment-aware lookup.
